title: Roadbook conformance case
description: A case.json: a machine, its input, the host's scripted behaviour and the expected final status. The expected trace is trace.jsonl next to it. See spec/conformance/README.md.

description.description: What the case checks, in a sentence or two.

requires.description: Features the case needs beyond the first version's. A runner skips a case that requires a feature it does not implement.

chart.description: The entry .road file, relative to spec/conformance. Its IR is the file next to it with .road replaced by .ir.json.

machine.description: The machine run as the root run, r1.

input.description: The machine's arguments, keyed by parameter name. A ref argument is the id of a top-level run already started, so the root run has none.

stub.description: Machines that are scripted like tasks instead of run from the chart when invoked.

fns.description: Results of the host's pure functions, keyed by function name, then by argument list. A call that is not listed fails the case.

actions.description: Action calls that have a host defect, keyed by action name, then by arguments. Every other action call does nothing and returns at once.

args.description: The arguments, keyed by parameter name.

defect.description: The message of the host defect every matching call has.

script.description: What happens after the root run starts, in order. The runner lets every run settle after each step.

status.description: The root run's status after the script.

advance.description: Advance virtual time by this many milliseconds, firing every timer that falls due on the way.

event.description: Give a top-level run an external event, as host code does: the root run, or the run named by run.

task.description: End the one running scripted invoke of this task (or stubbed machine): with done, fail or defect; or, with emit, have it emit one of its task's emits through its emitter and keep running. run picks the run when several have one, key the spawned one by its key, and as the invoke by its as name when one state runs the task twice.

as.description: The as name of the invoke meant, when a run has several running invokes of that name.

key.description: For a spawned task or a stubbed spawned child, the key of the one meant, when its run has several of that name.

defect.description: The message of a host defect.

emit.description: An event of the task's emits, which it emits through its emitter.

cancel.description: Cancel a top-level run from outside: the root run, or the run named by run.

start.description: Start another top-level run of a machine, as host code spawns one. run is its id: r2 for the first start step (or restore step that is not refused), r3 for the next, and so on. A ref argument is the id of a top-level run already started. status is the run's status after the last step.

snapshotName.description: A saved snapshot of the case: the file <name>.snapshot.json in the case's directory, in canonical JSON followed by a line feed.

snapshot.description: Save a top-level run (the root run, or the run named by run) as it is now, and compare the saved snapshot byte for byte with the file the name gives. The run carries on.

restore.description: Restore the saved snapshot the name gives as a new top-level run: run is its id, the next after the runs started before it, and status its status after the last step. With migrate, the host's migration returns the snapshot that name gives. With refused, the restore must be refused for that reason, and no run is started.

suspend.description: Suspend a top-level run (the root run, or the run named by run): once it is idle or has ended, which may be after later steps, compare the saved snapshot it gives byte for byte with the file the name gives.

together.description: Queue several inputs for one run before it takes the first of them, as when they arrive at the same moment. An advance item queues the expiries of the timers due in its window; an emit item the task.emitted input its invoke's emitter would push, or nothing.
